sections.executive_summary:
Texas licenses home health agencies as **Home and Community Support Services Agencies (HCSSAs)** under Health & Safety Code Chapter 142 and 26 TAC Chapter 558, and HHSC issues the license [S1][S3]. A skilled home health agency chooses between two categories. **Licensed Home Health Services (LHHS)** is state licensure only. **Licensed and Certified Home Health Services** is for Medicare-certified agencies. A Medicare-track applicant should request the licensed and certified category on its initial application: HHSC issues an interim license showing licensed home health services while CMS certification is pending, and adds the certified category automatically when CMS certifies the agency [S3]. Almost every agency that reaches profit does it through Medicare certification. Texas Medicaid, including its managed care plans, pays for home health only to agencies that are Medicare-certified and hold the 'licensed and certified' category [S30]. Check each Medicare Advantage plan's own credentialing criteria.

The state license is cheap and fairly quick: $2,625 for a three-year term [S2]. HHSC has up to 45 days to find a TULIP application complete and up to 45 more days to issue the license [S65]. The hard part is federal. An agency must serve **10 skilled patients (at least 7 active at the time of survey) before the Medicare survey** [S25]. It must also show **initial reserve operating funds** for three months of operation [S23], pay a $750 enrollment fee [S24], and in practice buy a deemed-status accreditation survey. CMS ranks initial HHA certification as Tier 4 (lowest) survey work, and HHSC says it is not doing initial Medicare surveys unless CMS agrees [S16][S26]. All of this happens before the agency can bill Medicare or Texas Medicaid for home health.

Once certified, the economics are strong. Medicare pays $2,038.22 per 30-day period nationally in CY 2026. In Houston that becomes $1,996.85 before case-mix and the 2% sequestration [S18][S20]. MedPAC reports a 21.2% FFS Medicare margin for freestanding agencies in 2024, but only a 5.0% all-payer margin, because Medicare Advantage and Medicaid pay less [S22]. The CY 2026 rule cut aggregate payments 1.3% [S17].

In this report's model, a Medicare-certified Houston agency **loses money at 25 and 50 active patients and is only thinly profitable at 100 patients** (about $2,100 a month, a 1.7% margin) with a 45/45/10 Medicare FFS / Medicare Advantage / Medicaid mix. That result depends on two assumptions: Medicare Advantage paying about $160 per visit (a published national benchmark, not a Texas contract rate [S64]) and lean field visit times (an operator estimate). If visits take 2.0 hours including drive and documentation, every modeled configuration loses money. A 50-patient agency loses money even with a Medicare-FFS-weighted mix. Profit in Texas takes scale, a Medicare FFS share of at least about 41% of patients at 100-patient scale, and tight visit productivity. A Medicaid personal-attendant-only agency is a different HCSSA category (Personal Assistance Services). It is not viable on the September 2025 STAR+PLUS rate alone at any modeled size.
sections.service_model:
### What a Texas home health agency is
An HCSSA provides home health, hospice or personal assistance services to people in their residence [S15]. Applicants choose one or more of six license categories [S3]:

1. Licensed and certified home health services (Medicare-certified)
2. Licensed and certified home health services with home dialysis designation
3. Licensed home health services
4. Licensed home health services with home dialysis designation
5. Hospice services
6. Personal assistance services (PAS)

An agency that requests the certified category on its initial application must also apply to CMS for Medicare certification. While it waits, HHSC issues the license with the **licensed home health** category, provided the agency follows the Medicare conditions of participation (42 CFR Part 484) as if it were already certified. HHSC adds the certified category once CMS certifies the agency [S3]. Personal-attendant-only agencies (non-skilled help with daily living) are licensed in the **PAS** category, not a home health category, and their administrator qualifications are lower [S4].

### Who is served
Medicare home health covers beneficiaries who are homebound and need part-time or intermittent skilled care [S22]. Nationally in 2024, a full 30-day period averaged 8.4 in-person visits: 4.1 skilled nursing, 3.8 therapy, and 0.5 aide or social work [S22]. Most referrals come from hospitals, post-acute discharges and physicians.

### Regulatory framework
- **State:** Health & Safety Code Ch. 142, 26 TAC Ch. 558 (licensing, administration, surveys), and Health & Safety Code Ch. 250 (criminal history and registry checks) [S3][S59].
- **Federal:** 42 CFR Part 484 (conditions of participation, OASIS), 42 CFR §489.28 (capitalization), and PDGM payment rules [S23][S27].
- **Medicaid:** 1 TAC §354.1033 requires Medicare certification for Medicaid home health [S30]. EVV has been mandatory for Medicaid home health care services since January 1, 2024 [S34].
- **Pending change:** HHSC proposed Chapter 558 amendments in the September 18, 2026 Texas Register. They would remove two-year renewal fees, add a teleservices rule, apply the existing 24-hour initial administrator training to all newly designated administrators and define the time frame to complete it, raise the initial alternate delivery site change-of-ownership fee from $1,000 to $1,500, and clarify the six-month initial survey deadline. The amendments are not final [S14].
sections.licensing_pathway:
### Step 1 — Form the entity and register
On the license application, a Medicare-track agency should request the **licensed and certified home health services** category from the start (see Step 5) [S3].

File a Certificate of Formation with the Texas Secretary of State (an LLC costs $300 on Form 205) [S58]. HHSC requires the applicant to be registered and in good standing with both the Secretary of State and the Comptroller [S1].

### Step 2 — Qualify leadership and complete Presurvey Training
The **administrator and alternate administrator** of a home health agency must be one of the following [S4]:
- a licensed physician, RN, licensed social worker, licensed therapist or licensed nursing home administrator with at least one year of health-related management or supervisory experience, or
- a high-school or GED graduate with two years of that experience.

The **supervising nurse and alternate** must be RNs licensed in Texas or under the Nurse Licensure Compact, with at least one year of RN experience in the last 36 months [S4]. The administrator, alternate administrator, supervising nurse and alternate supervising nurse must all finish HHSC's **Presurvey Training before the application is submitted** [S3]. Separately, a newly designated administrator needs **24 clock hours of administration training**. Eight of those hours must come before designation and 16 within the first 12 months [S5]. After that, 12 hours of continuing education are required each year [S6].

### Step 3 — Apply in TULIP and pay $2,625
Submit the application, required documents and the $2,625 initial fee (parent agency or branch) through TULIP [S1][S2]. Under 26 TAC §558.31, HHSC has up to **45 days** from submission to determine whether the application is complete, and up to **45 more days** to issue the license once it is complete, so plan on up to 90 days plus any time spent curing deficiencies [S65]. If HHSC finds deficiencies, you have **30 days** to respond or the application is denied [S1]. Fees are not refundable [S1][S2].

### Step 4 — Admit clients and request the initial state survey
Within **six months** of the license's effective date, the agency must admit and serve at least one client in its highest category. It must then submit **HHSC Form 2020, Notification of Readiness for Initial Survey**, listing each client's name, admission date and category [S7]. An agency accredited by ACHC, CHAP or The Joint Commission can instead send its accreditation documents within the same six months to be exempt from the survey [S7][S8].

### Step 5 — Medicare certification (the long pole)
- Enroll through **CMS-855A** in PECOS and pay the **$750** CY 2026 application fee [S24][S25].
- Show **initial reserve operating funds** covering the first three months of Medicare billing. At least 50% must be non-borrowed, and you need bank statements plus a bank-officer attestation [S23].
- Serve **10 skilled patients** (any payer) under the conditions of participation, with at least 7 active at the survey. Show that you can transmit OASIS data [S25].
- Get surveyed. Initial HHA certification is Tier 4 state survey work, and HHSC is not doing initial Medicare surveys unless CMS agrees. **Deemed accreditation is the practical route.** An accreditor may survey only after the MAC finishes its enrollment review and recommends approval [S16][S26].
- Because you requested the licensed and certified category on the initial application, HHSC adds it to the license once CMS certifies the agency; until then the license shows licensed home health services [S3].
- Contract a CMS-approved HHCAHPS survey vendor before the first Medicare patient (42 CFR §484.245(b)) [S72].

### Step 6 — Medicaid, Medicare Advantage and managed care
After certification, enroll in Texas Medicaid through TMHP [S30]. Then contract with STAR+PLUS, STAR Kids and Medicare Advantage plans, and onboard to EVV (HHAeXchange is the state-funded system) [S35].

### Renewal
The license term is three years, and renewal costs $2,625 [S2]. A complete renewal filed by day 45 before expiration avoids the late fee, which is half the renewal fee. The agency must have served at least one client during the license period [S12].
sections.reimbursement:
### Medicare fee-for-service (PDGM)
Medicare pays a case-mix- and wage-adjusted amount per **30-day period**. The CY 2026 national standardized amount is **$2,038.22** for agencies that report quality data and $1,998.41 for those that don't [S18]. The labor-related share is 74.9%, adjusted by the CBSA wage index [S18][S20]. Texas CY 2026 indexes are Houston 0.9729, Dallas 0.9639, Fort Worth 0.9691, Austin 0.9660, San Antonio 0.8526 and rural Texas 0.8400 [S20]. That makes a Houston period at case-mix 1.0 worth **$1,996.85**, or **$1,956.91** after the 2% sequestration, which remains in effect [S63]. The 432 PDGM case-mix weights range from 0.5364 to 1.9558 [S21].

CY 2026 changes: a 2.4% market-basket update, offset by a −1.023% permanent and a −3.0% one-year temporary behavioral adjustment and a fixed-dollar-loss ratio of 0.37. The net aggregate change is −1.3% [S17][S19]. Periods below the LUPA threshold of 2–5 visits are paid per visit: SN $176.96, PT $193.42, OT $194.74, SLP $210.25, aide $80.12, MSW $283.64 nationally [S18]. About 7% of periods were LUPAs in 2024 [S22]. Texas HHAs are in CMS's **Review Choice Demonstration** through 2029 and must choose pre-claim review, postpayment review, or minimal review with a 25% payment reduction [S22][S60].

### Medicare Advantage
In 2024, 53.5% of Texas's 4.77 million Medicare beneficiaries were in Medicare Advantage or other plans [S53]. MA plans pay either per visit or per episode, and contract rates aren't public. Agency payment from episodic MA plans is 'typically less' than traditional Medicare [S56]. Enhabit, a Dallas-based operator with 249 home health locations, says MA plans 'typically pay materially less than FFS Medicare' and its FY2025 10-K shows why: about $215 of home health revenue per Medicare visit versus about $160 per non-Medicare visit (MA, managed care and Medicaid combined), roughly 26% less [S64]. MA enrollees also receive about 11% fewer visits per user [S57]. For that reason MedPAC's all-payer margin (5.0%) is far below the FFS Medicare margin (21.2%) [S22].

### Texas Medicaid (FFS and managed care)
Medicaid home health requires Medicare certification [S30]. The TMHP FFS schedule pays **$98.92 per visit** for G0299 (RN) and G0300 (LVN) [S31]. Most Medicaid members are in managed care (STAR+PLUS for adults with disabilities and older adults, STAR Kids for children), and MCO contract rates are negotiated.

### Personal assistance (separate PAS category)
STAR+PLUS PAS (S5125 U3) pays **$4.40 per 15 minutes** ($17.60/hour) as of September 1, 2025. That is $3.71 attendant cost plus $0.69 administrative, built on the **$13.00** attendant base wage funded by GAA Rider 23 and 14% payroll taxes and benefits ($13 × 1.14 ÷ 4 = $3.71) [S32][S74]. THSteps children's PCS (T1019) is $4.26–$4.57 per 15 minutes, depending on modifier [S31].
sections.demand:
### Who generates referrals
Medicare home health referrals come mostly from hospital discharge planners, skilled nursing facility discharges, physicians and Medicare Advantage care managers. MedPAC reports steady FFS volume in 2024: 24.7 thirty-day periods per 100 FFS beneficiaries and about 3.1 full periods per user [S22].

### Texas population signals
- **Medicare:** 4,770,640 Texas beneficiaries in 2024, up from 4,286,051 in 2020. Medicare Advantage passed Original Medicare for the first time in 2024, at 53.5% [S53]. A new agency should expect roughly half its Medicare patients to be MA members.
- **Medicaid long-term services:** more than 198,000 Texans were on six HHSC interest lists in March 2026. Some waits for CLASS and HCS run 17–18 years [S54]. These are waiver lists, not home health waits, but they show strong unmet demand for attendant and in-home services once people are funded.
- **Supply:** 97% of FFS beneficiaries nationally live in a ZIP code served by two or more HHAs, and 86% by five or more [S22]. Texas metro markets are competitive. DSHS surveyed 435 Texas home health and hospice agencies with an annual census of 200 or more [S61]. That count leaves out smaller agencies.

### Where to compete
Without a sourced market-share dataset, this report makes no market-specific claims. The practical levers are clinical capability (wound care, cardiopulmonary, therapy-led orthopedic recovery), fast start of care (the RN initial assessment is due within 48 hours of referral [S29]), and MA and MCO network participation.
sections.operations:
### Staffing rules
- **Texas sets no staff-to-client ratios.** Chapter 558 requires written staffing policies: orientation, competency demonstration when a license or experience doesn't establish it, and pediatric competency [S10].
- The **administrator** manages daily operations and must be reachable during operating hours, with a written alternate. The **supervising nurse** must always be available to staff in person or by phone, with a written alternate [S9]. Medicare likewise requires the administrator or a pre-designated person, and a clinical manager, to be available during all operating hours [S27].
- **Assessments:** an RN initial assessment within 48 hours of referral, a comprehensive OASIS assessment within 5 days of start of care, an update in the last 5 days of every 60 days, and an assessment within 48 hours after a hospital return [S29].
- **Aides (Medicare):** at least 75 hours of training (16 classroom hours before 16 supervised practical hours), an RN competency evaluation, and 12 hours of in-service each year. A supervisory assessment is due at least every 14 days for patients receiving skilled services, and an RN on-site visit every 60 days otherwise [S28].
- **Employability:** before hire and before first client contact, run the criminal history check and search the Nurse Aide Registry and Employee Misconduct Registry. Repeat the registry searches at least every 12 months, and immediately discharge anyone found unemployable [S11][S59].

### Required systems
- **OASIS-capable EMR.** You must show OASIS transmission before the initial certification survey [S25].
- **EVV** for Medicaid home health care services (since January 1, 2024) and personal care. HHAeXchange is the state-funded EVV system [S34][S35].
- **TULIP** for licensing and **PECOS** for Medicare enrollment [S1].

### Wages (BLS OEWS 2025, Texas)
Texas medians: RN $46.14 (Houston $48.00), LVN $29.92 (Houston $30.61), PT $50.87, PTA $37.50, OT $51.03, SLP $48.03, healthcare social worker $33.65, home health aide $11.65 (75th percentile $13.23) [S36]–[S43]. All modeled wages exceed the $7.25 Texas minimum wage, which is tied to the federal rate [S47][S48]. **Workers' compensation is elective for Texas private employers** [S49]. The new-employer unemployment tax rate is 2.70% on the first $9,000 of wages [S50].
sections.market_conditions:
### Payment trend
Medicare FFS remains profitable for freestanding agencies: a 21.2% margin in 2024 (5.7% at the 25th percentile, 31.0% at the 75th) and a projected 19% in 2026 [S22]. Even so, CMS is still applying budget-neutrality cuts: −1.023% permanent and −3.0% temporary in CY 2026 [S17]. MedPAC recommended a further 7% base-rate reduction for 2027 [S22]. Agencies in the top volume quintile earned a 23.2% FFS margin, versus 14.4% in the bottom quintile. Scale matters [S22].

### Payer mix pressure
Medicare Advantage now covers most Texas beneficiaries [S53]. MA patients get fewer visits [S57], and MA agency payments are typically below traditional Medicare [S56]. The national all-payer margin is just 5.0% [S22].

### Visit intensity
Visits per full period fell from 10.2 (2019) to 8.4 (2024), mostly therapy, while payment per visit rose from $180 to $245 [S22]. As a cost benchmark, Enhabit reported a 2025 home health cost of service of $97.70 per visit (payroll, benefits, travel, supplies and branch leases) [S64]. That benefits agencies that manage visit utilization well.

### Labor
Licensed clinicians are the main cost: RN median $46.14/hour in Texas [S36]. Aide wages are low (median $11.65) [S38]. Personal attendant rates are built on a $13.00 attendant base wage (GAA Rider 23) [S74], so PAS-only agencies compete for the same workforce at very thin margins.

### Program integrity
Texas is in the Review Choice Demonstration through 2029 [S22], and CMS is expanding retroactive revocation authority [S17]. New agencies should budget for clean documentation from day one.
sections.financial_narrative:
### How the P&L is built
The unit is one **active patient**. One patient-month is treated as one 30-day period, and capacity is the target active census that the fixed staff can support. The 90% default occupancy is an operator assumption. Revenue per patient-month blends the payers:

- **Medicare FFS full period:** $1,956.91. This is the Houston wage-adjusted CY 2026 period at case-mix 1.0 after the 2% sequestration [S18][S20][S63]. It applies to 93% of FFS periods.
- **Medicare FFS LUPA period:** $509.70, which is 3 SN visits at the Houston-adjusted per-visit rate after sequestration. It applies to the 7% of FFS periods that are LUPAs [S18][S22].
- **Medicare Advantage:** 7.5 visits (8.4 × 0.89 [S22][S57]) at **$159.57 per visit**. Texas MA contract rates are not published, so this is an assumption anchored to a published benchmark: Enhabit's FY2025 home health non-Medicare revenue per visit ($813.8 million × 44.1% non-Medicare ÷ 2,249,095 non-Medicare visits) [S64]. It is a national figure that blends MA with commercial managed care and Medicaid. Your own contracts may pay more or less.
- **Texas Medicaid:** about 4 visits at $98.92 (TMHP G0299/G0300) [S31].

Default mix is 45% Medicare FFS, 45% MA, 10% Medicaid, which reflects Texas's 53.5% MA share [S53]. A Medicare-FFS-weighted alternative uses 70/20/10.

### Costs
**Visit labor** scales with census. It uses Houston median wages [S36]–[S43] and the 8.4-visit MedPAC discipline mix [S22] at 1.25–1.5 hours per visit including documentation and drive. **The hours per visit are an operator estimate — verify locally**; no citable productivity standard was found. **Fixed salaries** use Houston OEWS 2025 wages: administrator $124,400 (Houston median) [S44], supervising nurse / clinical manager required by §558.243 and §484.105 at the Houston RN 75th percentile ($116,000) [S9][S27][S36], intake and scheduling ($44,210 each) [S46] and billing / OASIS coding ($51,250 each) [S45].

Payroll burden is FICA 7.65% [S51] plus Texas and federal unemployment tax [S50] (8.5% combined), an elective workers' comp line [S49] and benefits (both operator estimates). Mileage is reimbursed at the 2026 IRS rate of $0.725 per mile [S52]. Office space is 1,800 sq ft of Houston Class B space at $23.23/sq ft/yr gross [S55]. The license renewal is amortized at $2,625 over 36 months [S2]. The model includes the mandatory **HHCAHPS survey vendor** required of Medicare-certified agencies by 42 CFR §484.245(b) [S72] at $300 a month (operator estimate — vendor quote required). Software, insurance, accreditation and professional fees are labeled operator estimates.

### What the configurations show (90% of target census)
- **25 patients:** about $32k revenue a month against about $31k of burdened fixed salaries before any visit labor. Loses about $24.9k a month, typical of the certification ramp.
- **50 patients, 45/45/10 mix:** loses about $11.0k a month.
- **50 patients, Medicare-FFS-weighted (70/20/10):** loses about $3.6k a month.
- **100 patients, 45/45/10:** **thinly profitable, about $2,130 a month (1.7% net margin)**. It breaks even at about 87 billable patients. At the conservative 80% it loses about $5.2k a month; at 100% it earns about $9.4k.
- **PAS-only agency (STAR+PLUS PAS, 50 clients):** loses about $21.3k a month. After the attendant's wage and burden there is almost no margin left in a $17.60/hour rate.

### Medicare Advantage rate sensitivity
The 100-patient configuration breaks even when MA pays **about $152.56 per visit**, only about $7 (4.4%) below the modeled $159.57. An MA book that pays less than that, or uses fewer visits per period, turns the default configuration into a loss. The same 100-patient agency with a 70/20/10 mix earns about $17.0k a month, and it breaks even once Medicare FFS reaches about 41% of patients.

### Visit-time sensitivity (2.0 hours per visit)
Because visit hours are an operator estimate, the model was rerun at **2.0 hours per visit** for every discipline, including drive and documentation (16.8 field hours per patient-month instead of 11.6). **Every configuration loses money:** 100 patients 45/45/10 about −$21.4k a month; 100 patients at 70/20/10 about −$6.6k; 50 patients 70/20/10 about −$15.4k; 50 patients 45/45/10 about −$22.8k; 25 patients about −$30.8k. At 2.0 hours, a 100-patient agency would need about 81% of patients on Medicare FFS, or about 136 billable patients on the same fixed team, to break even. The 100-patient configuration breaks even at about 1.44 hours per visit on average, against the modeled 1.38. For comparison, the model's field cost is about $82 per visit (labor, mileage and supplies), while Enhabit reported $97.70 per visit in 2025, a figure that also includes branch leases [S64]. Measure your clinicians' real visits per day before you commit.

Startup costs include the **initial reserve operating funds** CMS requires (42 CFR §489.28) and the cost of serving 10 pre-certification patients who can't be billed to Medicare or Medicaid [S23][S25][S30].
sections.risks:
1. **Certification delay.** No Medicare or Medicaid home health billing is possible until certification [S30]. State initial surveys are Tier 4, so deemed accreditation is the practical route, and an accreditor can survey only after the MAC recommends approval [S16][S26]. Budget 6–12+ months of fixed costs; this is an operator estimate, since no official average exists.
2. **Capitalization.** CMS can deny or revoke billing privileges if reserve funds aren't kept through the first three months of billing [S23].
3. **Pre-certification patients.** You need 10 skilled patients (7 active) before survey, and they cannot be Medicare- or Medicaid-billed [S25][S30].
4. **Rate cuts.** CY 2026 is −1.3% aggregate, with a −3.0% temporary adjustment [S17]. MedPAC recommends a further 7% cut for 2027 [S22].
5. **Medicare Advantage rates.** MA pays less and uses fewer visits [S56][S57][S64]. The model's $159.57 per MA visit is a national benchmark, not a Texas contract rate. The default 100-patient configuration breaks even at about $152.56 per MA visit, so a contract only about 4% below the benchmark wipes out its profit. Model every MA contract against your own cost per visit before signing.
6. **Case-mix risk.** Late or community-admission periods carry lower weights, averaging about 0.83 for late community admissions [S21].
7. **Review Choice Demonstration** claim review in Texas through 2029 [S22][S60].
8. **Compliance.** Registry and criminal history violations require immediate discharge [S11][S59]. Renewal requires serving at least one client per license period [S12]. Proposed Chapter 558 changes are pending [S14].
9. **Workers' comp.** Coverage is elective in Texas [S49], but going without it exposes the agency to employee injury lawsuits. Get insurance and legal advice.
10. **Labor.** RN and therapist wages drive margins [S36][S39].
11. **Visit productivity.** Hours per visit are an operator estimate. At 2.0 hours per visit including drive and documentation, every modeled configuration loses money (100 patients: about −$21.4k a month). Track visits per clinician per day from the first month.
12. **HHCAHPS and quality reporting.** A CMS-approved HHCAHPS vendor is mandatory (42 CFR §484.245(b)) [S72]; missing quality data costs a 2-point lower update [S18].
sections.recommendations:
1. **Request the licensed and certified home health services category on the initial application**; HHSC issues an interim licensed home health license until CMS certifies you [S3]. Run the agency to Part 484 standards from the first patient.
2. **Fund the gap before applying.** Combine the CMS initial reserve operating funds (at least 50% non-borrowed) with at least two quarters of fixed costs and the cost of the 10 pre-certification patients [S23][S25].
3. **Choose deemed accreditation (ACHC, CHAP or The Joint Commission) for Medicare certification**, and time it right after the MAC's 855A recommendation [S16][S26]. Accreditation also exempts you from HHSC routine licensing surveys [S8].
4. **Size for at least 100 active patients** within 18–24 months, and treat 100 as the floor, not the goal: at 100 patients the default mix earns only about 1.7%. Smaller agencies in this model don't cover the required administrator, supervising nurse and billing overhead. MedPAC data show margins rise with volume [S22].
5. **Prioritize Medicare FFS and high-acuity referrals.** Early community and institutional admissions carry higher case-mix weights (about 1.16–1.36 on average) [S21]. Negotiate MA contracts on an episodic basis where possible, and model each one [S56].
6. **Keep visits efficient.** The 100-patient model breaks even at about 1.44 hours per visit including drive and documentation, so route clinicians tightly by geography and use point-of-care documentation. Use LVNs and PTAs under RN and PT supervision, and watch LUPA risk, since thresholds are 2–5 visits [S18][S22].
7. **Contract with STAR+PLUS and STAR Kids MCOs and onboard to HHAeXchange EVV** once certified [S30][S35]. Treat Medicaid as a census stabilizer, not a margin driver.
8. **Add PAS only as a complement** to referral relationships, not as a stand-alone business [S32].
9. **Build compliance for the Review Choice Demonstration** from day one [S60].
10. **Keep Medicare FFS at roughly 40% or more of patients** at 100-patient scale (the model breaks even at about 41%), and don't sign MA contracts below about $152 per visit without an episodic rate or volume that offsets it [S64].

checklist.task: Form a Texas legal entity (LLC, corporation or nonprofit)
checklist.instructions: File a Certificate of Formation with the Texas Secretary of State through SOSDirect. An LLC uses Form 205 and costs $300. Online filings usually process in a few business days.
checklist.cite: Tex. Bus. Org. Code; SOS Form 205

checklist.task: Obtain an EIN from the IRS
checklist.instructions: Apply online at irs.gov (free, issued immediately). You need it for payroll, banking, TULIP, PECOS and TMHP.

checklist.task: Register with the Texas Comptroller and confirm good standing
checklist.instructions: HHSC requires the applicant to be registered and in good standing with the Comptroller before it approves a license. Set up a franchise tax account.

checklist.task: Confirm good standing with the Texas Secretary of State
checklist.instructions: HHSC checks Secretary of State status before approving the license. Keep the registered agent current.

checklist.task: Register with TWC for state unemployment tax
checklist.instructions: The 2026 new-employer rate is 2.70% on the first $9,000 of each employee's wages. Register before the first payroll.

checklist.task: Decide on workers' compensation coverage
checklist.instructions: Coverage is elective for Texas private employers. Nonsubscribers lose certain legal defenses in injury suits and have notice duties to TDI and employees. Get a broker quote and legal advice.

checklist.task: Choose license categories
checklist.instructions: For a Medicare-track agency, request the licensed and certified home health services category on the initial application. HHSC issues the license with the licensed home health services category while you wait for CMS, you must follow 42 CFR Part 484 as if certified, and HHSC adds the certified category when CMS certifies you (26 TAC §558.13(d)). Add PAS only if you will provide attendant care. Home dialysis designation is optional.

checklist.task: Open a business bank account and plan capitalization
checklist.instructions: Medicare certification requires initial reserve operating funds covering the first three months after billing privileges begin, with at least 50% non-borrowed. Line up owner equity and any line of credit early.

checklist.task: Designate a qualified administrator and alternate administrator
checklist.instructions: Each must be a licensed physician, RN, licensed social worker, licensed therapist or licensed NHA with 1 year of health-related management or supervisory experience, or a high-school/GED graduate with 2 years of that experience. Both must read, write and comprehend English and have no barring convictions.

checklist.task: Designate a supervising nurse and alternate supervising nurse
checklist.instructions: Each must be an RN licensed in Texas or under the Nurse Licensure Compact with at least 1 year of RN experience in the last 36 months. Home dialysis agencies have higher requirements.

checklist.task: Complete HHSC Presurvey Training (administrator, alternate, supervising nurse, alternate)
checklist.instructions: This is required before submitting the license application. For home health categories, the supervising nurse and alternate must also complete it. Save the completion certificates.

checklist.task: Complete 8 hours of administrator training before designation
checklist.instructions: These are the first 8 of 24 required hours, completed in the 12 months before designation. Topics: licensing standards and applicable state and federal law (HSC Ch. 142 and 250, ADA, FMLA, OSHA and others).

checklist.task: Schedule the remaining 16 hours of administrator training within 12 months
checklist.instructions: Topics include fraud and abuse prevention, advance directives, client rights, complaint resolution, emergency preparedness, abuse/neglect/exploitation, infection control and OASIS (home health).

checklist.task: Set up annual administrator continuing education tracking
checklist.instructions: 12 clock hours in each 12-month period from the designation date, covering at least two of the listed topics. Presurvey Training hours don't count toward it.

checklist.task: Document the governing body, administrator and clinical manager structure for Medicare
checklist.instructions: The administrator reports to the governing body. A clinical manager must be available during all operating hours, and a written pre-designated alternate is required.

checklist.task: Lease office space in your service area
checklist.instructions: Size for administration, secure records and staff work areas. Houston Class B office space averaged $23.23 per sq ft per year (gross) in Q2 2026. Confirm zoning and certificate of occupancy with the city before signing.

checklist.task: Bind general and professional liability insurance
checklist.instructions: Chapter 558 sets no dollar minimum, but MA, MCO and referral contracts usually require coverage. Get at least three quotes. Premiums in the model are operator estimates.

checklist.task: Select an OASIS-capable home health EMR
checklist.instructions: New HHAs must show they can transmit OASIS before the initial certification survey. Register for OASIS submission credentials through the state OASIS coordinator.

checklist.task: Plan EVV onboarding for Medicaid services
checklist.instructions: EVV has been required for Medicaid home health care services since January 1, 2024, and for personal care. HHAeXchange is the state-funded system. Submit the onboarding form when you enroll in Medicaid.
checklist.cite: 21st Century Cures Act §12006; HHSC EVV policy

checklist.task: Set up payroll with correct tax withholding
checklist.instructions: FICA is 7.65% employer share. Register for TWC unemployment tax. Reimburse mileage up to the 2026 IRS rate of 72.5 cents per mile.

checklist.task: Set up business records and solvency controls
checklist.instructions: Keep enough funds for payroll, never pay staff with insufficient-funds checks, and keep original dated records that HHSC can review on request.

checklist.task: Write staffing policies (orientation, competency, pediatrics)
checklist.instructions: Include orientation to agency policies, competency demonstration when education, license or experience doesn't establish it, and pediatric competency if you serve children. Chapter 558 sets no staffing ratios.

checklist.task: Write assessment and plan-of-care policies to Medicare timelines
checklist.instructions: RN initial assessment within 48 hours of referral; comprehensive OASIS assessment within 5 days of start of care; update in the last 5 days of every 60 days and within 48 hours of a hospital return; discharge assessment.

checklist.task: Write a home health aide training, competency and supervision policy
checklist.instructions: 75-hour training (16 classroom hours before 16 supervised practical hours), RN competency evaluation, 12 hours of in-service a year, supervisory assessment every 14 days for skilled patients, RN on-site visit every 60 days otherwise.

checklist.task: Write an employability verification policy
checklist.instructions: Criminal history check under HSC Ch. 250. Search the NAR and EMR before hire or first client contact and at least every 12 months. Discharge immediately if someone is found unemployable. Keep the results in personnel files.

checklist.task: Write administrator and supervising nurse availability and alternate designation procedures
checklist.instructions: The administrator or alternate must be reachable during operating hours. The supervising nurse must always be available in person or by phone. Designate both alternates in writing.

checklist.task: Write an emergency preparedness plan
checklist.instructions: This is required under the Chapter 558 agency administration rules (§558.256) and the Medicare CoPs. Cover communication, patient triage by acuity and continuity of operations.

checklist.task: Write abuse, neglect and exploitation reporting and investigation policies
checklist.instructions: Address self-reported incidents (§558.249) and agency investigations (§558.250). Cover staff training on recognizing and reporting.

checklist.task: Write a QAPI program, infection control, patient rights and clinical records policies
checklist.instructions: Required under the Medicare home health CoPs in 42 CFR Part 484. Accreditors review these at the deemed-status survey.

checklist.task: Write billing, insurance claims and anti-solicitation policies
checklist.instructions: Chapter 558 covers billing and insurance claims (§558.254) and prohibits soliciting patients (§558.255). Align them with the Review Choice Demonstration documentation process.

checklist.task: Create a TULIP account and complete the initial license application
checklist.instructions: Submit the application online through TULIP and upload every required document. Use the legal name exactly as filed with the Secretary of State.

checklist.task: Pay the $2,625 initial license fee
checklist.instructions: The fee applies to the parent agency (and to each branch). An alternate delivery site is $1,000. The fee is non-refundable even if the application is denied or withdrawn. Pending: the September 18, 2026 proposal would raise the initial alternate delivery site change-of-ownership license fee from $1,000 to $1,500; not final [S14].

checklist.task: Respond to any deficiency notice within 30 days
checklist.instructions: HHSC posts deficiencies in TULIP. If you don't respond within 30 days, the application is denied. The §558.31 processing time frames (45 days to completeness, then 45 days to issue) run from a complete response.

checklist.task: Receive the license and record its effective date (HHSC: up to 45 days to find the application complete, then up to 45 days to issue)
checklist.instructions: Under §558.31, HHSC has up to 45 days from submission to determine the application is complete and up to 45 more days to issue the license, so plan on up to 90 days plus any time you take to cure deficiencies. The six-month clock to admit clients and request the initial survey starts on the license effective date. Calendar the deadline immediately.

checklist.task: Watch the proposed Chapter 558 amendments
checklist.instructions: The September 18, 2026 proposal changes fees, teleservices, administrator training and the initial survey rules. Check the Texas Register for the adoption date.

checklist.task: Run criminal history checks for unlicensed staff with client contact
checklist.instructions: Run checks under HSC Chapter 250. Anyone whose check is pending must have no direct client contact until it is complete.

checklist.task: Search the Nurse Aide Registry and Employee Misconduct Registry before hire
checklist.instructions: Search on the HHSC website before hire or first client contact. Applicants listed as unemployable cannot be hired.

checklist.task: Recruit field RNs, LVNs, therapists and aides at market wages
checklist.instructions: Texas 2025 medians: RN $46.14, LVN $29.92, PT $50.87, PTA $37.50, OT $51.03, SLP $48.03, aide $11.65. Every wage must be at least the $7.25 minimum wage.

checklist.task: Verify clinician licenses (BON, therapy boards) and aide training
checklist.instructions: Supervising nurse qualifications are in §558.244(c). Medicare aides need 75-hour training or competency evaluation per §484.80.

checklist.task: Create personnel files and orientation records
checklist.instructions: Include orientation, competency, license verification, registry results and criminal history results.

checklist.phase: PHASE 7 — FIRST CLIENTS & STATE INITIAL SURVEY
checklist.task: Admit and serve at least one home health client
checklist.instructions: Before Medicare certification you can't bill Medicare or Texas Medicaid for home health. Early clients will be private pay, commercial insurance or charity care.

checklist.phase: PHASE 7 — FIRST CLIENTS & STATE INITIAL SURVEY
checklist.task: Submit HHSC Form 2020 (Notification of Readiness for Initial Survey) within 6 months
checklist.instructions: Send it to the designated survey office with each client's name, admission date and category of service. Have the client list, client records, all policies and personnel records ready.

checklist.phase: PHASE 7 — FIRST CLIENTS & STATE INITIAL SURVEY
checklist.task: Or submit accreditation documentation within 6 months for survey exemption
checklist.instructions: Agencies accredited by The Joint Commission, CHAP or ACHC for their license category can send proof of accreditation instead of requesting the state survey.

checklist.phase: PHASE 7 — FIRST CLIENTS & STATE INITIAL SURVEY
checklist.task: Host the survey and submit any plan of correction
checklist.instructions: Run a mock survey first. Answer deficiencies in writing by the deadline the surveyor gives.

checklist.task: Submit CMS-855A in PECOS and pay the $750 application fee
checklist.instructions: Include ownership and managing employee disclosures. The MAC reviews enrollment and recommends approval to CMS before any accreditation survey.

checklist.task: Document initial reserve operating funds
checklist.instructions: Provide account statements, a bank-officer attestation and proof that cash equivalents are available. At least 50% must be non-borrowed. Any line of credit needs a letter of credit from an unrelated lender. Keep the funds through the first 3 months of billing.

checklist.task: Contract with a CMS-approved accrediting organization for deemed status
checklist.instructions: Choose ACHC, CHAP or The Joint Commission. HHSC is not doing initial Medicare surveys unless CMS agrees, and initial HHA certification is Tier 4 state work, so accreditation is the fastest route. Get fee quotes.

checklist.task: Serve 10 skilled patients under the CoPs (at least 7 active at survey)
checklist.instructions: Patients don't have to be Medicare patients. Collect and transmit OASIS where required. Show OASIS transmission before the survey.

checklist.task: Pass the deemed-status survey and receive the CMS tie-in / provider agreement
checklist.instructions: The effective date can't be earlier than the date all federal requirements are met (SOM Ch. 2 §2008D). Notify HHSC so it adds the licensed and certified home health category (26 TAC §558.13(d) [S3]).

checklist.task: Make your Review Choice Demonstration selection
checklist.instructions: Texas HHAs choose pre-claim review, postpayment review, or minimal review with a 25% payment reduction. The demonstration runs through 2029.

checklist.task: Set up HHVBP and HH QRP quality reporting
checklist.instructions: Agencies that don't submit quality data get a 2-point lower update; the CY 2026 national period is $1,998.41 versus $2,038.22. Track the expanded HHVBP measures.

checklist.task: Contract an approved HHCAHPS survey vendor before the first Medicare patient
checklist.instructions: Medicare-certified HHAs must contract with a CMS-approved, independent HHCAHPS survey vendor; only agencies with fewer than 60 eligible unique patients a year can claim an exemption. Missing HH QRP data costs a 2-point lower payment update. Pricing is not public, so get vendor quotes; the model carries an operator estimate.

checklist.phase: PHASE 9 — MEDICAID, MCO & MEDICARE ADVANTAGE CONTRACTING
checklist.task: Enroll in Texas Medicaid through TMHP
checklist.instructions: Requires Medicare certification and the licensed and certified home health category. The FFS fee schedule pays $98.92 per G0299/G0300 visit.

checklist.phase: PHASE 9 — MEDICAID, MCO & MEDICARE ADVANTAGE CONTRACTING
checklist.task: Credential with STAR+PLUS and STAR Kids MCOs in your service area
checklist.instructions: Rates are negotiated. Use the TMHP FFS and HHSC STAR+PLUS rate sheets as reference points.

checklist.phase: PHASE 9 — MEDICAID, MCO & MEDICARE ADVANTAGE CONTRACTING
checklist.task: Onboard to HHAeXchange EVV
checklist.instructions: MCOs reject Medicaid home health claims without matching EVV visits.

checklist.phase: PHASE 9 — MEDICAID, MCO & MEDICARE ADVANTAGE CONTRACTING
checklist.task: Negotiate Medicare Advantage contracts
checklist.instructions: 53.5% of Texas beneficiaries were in MA or other plans in 2024. Compare episodic vs per-visit offers against your own cost per visit, and model each contract before signing.

checklist.phase: PHASE 9 — MEDICAID, MCO & MEDICARE ADVANTAGE CONTRACTING
checklist.task: Optional: add the PAS category for STAR+PLUS attendant services
checklist.instructions: PAS (S5125 U3) pays $4.40 per 15 minutes as of 9/1/2025, built on the $13.00 attendant base wage funded by GAA Rider 23 plus 14% payroll taxes and benefits ($13 × 1.14 ÷ 4 = $3.71 attendant cost + $0.69 administrative) [S74]. Margins are thin, so add it only as a complement to home health.

checklist.task: Renew the license every 3 years ($2,625)
checklist.instructions: File a complete renewal by day 45 before expiration to avoid the late fee (half the renewal fee). You must have served at least one client during the license period.

checklist.task: Repeat NAR and EMR searches every 12 months
checklist.instructions: Keep a copy of each annual search. Discharge immediately anyone listed as unemployable.

checklist.task: Track administrator continuing education (12 hours a year)
checklist.instructions: Applies to the administrator and alternate. Keep certificates.

checklist.task: Track aide in-service (12 hours a year) and supervisory visits
checklist.instructions: Supervisory assessments every 14 days for skilled patients; RN visit every 60 days for non-skilled patients.

corrections_vs_previous: Old report put Medicare home health payment at about $3,000–$4,500 per 30-day episode. CY 2026 national standardized period is $2,038.22. Houston at case-mix 1.0 is $1,996.85, or $1,956.91 after sequestration (CMS CR 13488; CY 2026 wage index).

Old report listed staff-to-client ratios (1:8 skilled nursing, 1:4 personal care, 1:5 therapy) citing 26 TAC Ch. 558. Chapter 558 sets no staffing ratios; §558.245 requires only written staffing, orientation and competency policies.

Old report said administrators need a bachelor's degree, 2 years of experience and a nursing home administrator license. §558.244 requires a licensed physician, RN, LSW, licensed therapist or LNHA with 1 year of management experience, or HS/GED with 2 years.
Old report gave three different license fees ($2,625, '$500' and a '$200–$1,500' startup line) plus 'annual renewal fees'. §558.3: $2,625 initial and $2,625 per three-year renewal.

Old report described a mandatory pre-licensure site visit and a 60-day review. Under 26 TAC §558.31, HHSC has up to 45 days to find the application complete and up to 45 more days to issue the license; the survey happens after clients are admitted, requested on Form 2020 within 6 months (§558.521).

Old report modeled revenue as $90/hour × 15 hours/month per client and claimed break-even at 21 clients. Medicare pays per 30-day period under PDGM, not hourly. The break-even and startup totals ($93,950–$152,600) were built on that fabricated rate and left out CMS capitalization (42 CFR §489.28).
Old report and checklist called workers' compensation 'Texas-mandated' or tied it to W-2 status. Coverage is elective for Texas private employers (Labor Code §406.002).

Old report presented CLASS, TxHmL and STAR+PLUS waivers as primary home health funding and listed unverified waiver numbers and MCO names. Texas Medicaid home health requires Medicare certification and the licensed and certified category (1 TAC §354.1033); waiver numbers and MCO names have been removed as unverified.

Old P&L was a Mississippi template. It used a CY 2025 base of $2,030.86 (CMS shows $2,057.35), a 76.1% labor share (CY 2026: 74.9%), and a made-up Texas 'state wage index' of 0.89 (Medicare uses CBSA indexes: Houston 0.9729, Dallas 0.9639, rural Texas 0.8400). It ignored the 2% sequestration and priced Medicaid at an unsourced '75% of Medicare'. Texas Medicaid G0299/G0300 is $98.92 per visit.

Old checklist cited §558.259 for administrator qualifications and Presurvey CBT. Qualifications are §558.244; Presurvey Training is required by §558.13(a) before applying, and for home health also by the supervising nurse and alternate. §558.259 is the 24-hour administrator training (8 hours before designation, 16 within 12 months).

Old checklist left out the whole Medicare certification pathway: CMS-855A, the $750 fee, initial reserve operating funds, 10 skilled patients with 7 active, OASIS transmission, deemed accreditation, and the Review Choice Demonstration.
Old checklist stated a required $1,000,000 general liability minimum. No insurance minimum was found in 26 TAC Chapter 558; coverage limits are set by contracts and the operator's risk choices.

Prior audit note: '8-hour pre-licensing training per §558.260' is imprecise. §558.259 requires 24 hours (8 before designation, 16 within the first year); §558.260 is the 12-hour annual CE. HHSC Presurvey Training is a separate requirement under §558.13(a).
